system_prompt: You are an expert researcher extracting structured information from papers about Survey of large language models (LLMs) for biomedicine in Biomedical informatics and health AI. Extract only information supported by the provided paper text.
user_prompt_template:
Extract information from the paper using these fields:

1. datasets_used (Text, optional): Biomedical datasets, corpora, benchmarks, or data sources used to train, fine-tune, validate, or evaluate the LLM or related system. Example: PubMed abstracts, MIMIC-III clinical notes, MedQA, BioASQ
2. methods (Text, optional): The LLM approach, model architecture, prompting strategy, fine-tuning method, retrieval setup, or experimental design used in the study. Example: Zero-shot prompting with GPT-4; retrieval-augmented generation using PubMed articles
3. key_findings (Text, optional): Main results, conclusions, or notable observations reported by the paper about LLM performance or utility in biomedicine. Example: The model improved clinical question answering accuracy and produced more fluent summaries, but hallucinations remained common
4. evaluation_metrics (Text, optional): Metrics or criteria used to assess performance, quality, safety, or usefulness of the LLM system. Example: Accuracy, F1 score, ROUGE, BLEU, exact match, human expert rating
5. biomedical_task (Text, optional): The specific biomedical or clinical task addressed by the LLM study. Example: Clinical question answering, medical text summarization, diagnosis support, information extraction
6. llm_model_or_family (Text, optional): The large language model(s) or model family evaluated or discussed in the paper. Example: ChatGPT, GPT-4, BioGPT, LLaMA, Med-PaLM
7. biomedical_domain_context (Text, optional): The biomedical subdomain or health AI setting in which the LLM is applied. Example: Radiology, oncology, electronic health records, biomedical literature mining
8. study_type (Text, optional): The publication or study design relevant to evidence synthesis. Example: Benchmark evaluation, clinical validation, user study, review, methodological paper
9. comparison_baselines (Text, optional): Any baseline models, alternative methods, or human comparators used for comparison. Example: Compared against BERT, traditional machine learning models, and physician annotations
10. limitations_or_risks (Text, optional): Reported limitations, failure modes, safety concerns, or risks associated with the LLM approach in biomedicine. Example: Hallucinations, limited generalizability, privacy concerns, bias in clinical recommendations

Return ONLY valid JSON with exactly these schema field names. Use empty strings for unavailable optional values.

PAPER CONTENT:
{paper_text}
